name: pay-first-won
about: One concept clearly did well over many leads and one spent for nothing.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Our ads with hook pay_first (pay first) and scene equipment_on_road (truck on the road) spent $612.40 in the last 28 days over 48210 impressions and brought 31 leads, $19.75 per lead.
Our ads with hook life_first (life first) and scene home_street (home street) spent $188.00 in the last 28 days over 15120 impressions and brought no lead.
Of 31 of our ad leads in the last 28 days, 29 were called and 22 were reached.

output.audience: Class A flatbed drivers who meet the experience requirement and run, or want to run, Midwest regional lanes. Many are likely out longer than they want or sharing trucks at a larger fleet. A plain pay per mile, home weekly and an assigned truck would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, over a flatbed rolling on a Midwest road.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile, and the work is flatbed on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: This hook and scene brought all our earlier leads at a cost per lead under the benchmark's pause line, so build on it. Still is the only format; formats are unmeasured.

angles.idea: Say plainly who the job is for: the experience required, the Midwest lanes, and a small fleet that knows its drivers.
angles.proof: The job states an experience requirement, Midwest lanes and a small fleet where dispatch knows your name.
angles.why: Lead outcomes show how many leads were reached, not who qualified. Stating the requirement and area up front screens before the call. This concept is unmeasured.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck: a flatbed rig parked and waiting for its driver.
angles.proof: The job lists an assigned truck and flatbed work.
angles.why: An assigned truck is a concrete fact a flatbed driver can weigh against a current seat. No earlier ad of ours used this hook and scene, so nothing is measured.

angles.idea: Set the terms out as a plain list on a plain ground: the pay per mile, home weekly, the retirement plan.
angles.proof: Each line is a stated fact of the opening: the pay per mile, home weekly and the retirement plan.
angles.why: Home time is carried here because our home street ads spent and brought no lead, so that concept is left out. This concept itself is unmeasured.
